children.translated_text: Oṃ, salutation to you, O god of gods! O <s>Ekaśṛṅga</s> (single-horned one)! O you worshipped by the bull (<s>Dharma</s>)! O tree of the ocean! O <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>! O drinker of <s>Soma</s>! O blameless one! O auspicious one! O <s>Kapila</s>! O <s>Viṣvaksena</s>! O immovable one! O <s>Dharma</s>! O <s>Dharmadhvaja</s> (banner of righteousness)! O <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>! O <s>Vṛṣāvarta</s>! O you without beginning, middle, or end! O beloved of people! O born of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan! O you who recline in immortality! O eternal one! O you of triple abode! O <s>Tridhāman</s>! O <s>Tuṣita</s>! O <s>Dundubhi</s> (drum)! O world of the great! O navel of the worlds! O <s>Padmanābha</s> (lotus-naveled one)! O <s>Viriñca</s>! O you of many forms! O imperishable one! O consumer of oblations! O you who wield the broken axe! O <s>Cakra</s> (discus)! O <s>Muṇḍakeśa</s>! O <s>Haṃsa</s> (swan)! O greatly generous one! O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (lord of the senses)! O subtle one! O assemblage of great sages! O you free from passion and darkness! O foundation of all worlds! O <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>! O <s>Atapā</s>! O first-born! O born of <s>Dharma</s>! O navel of <s>Dharma</s>! O you whose navel is of rays! O <s>Candraratha</s> (moon-charioted)! O sinless one! You alone! O you who dwell in the ocean! O unborn one! O <s>Ekapāt</s> (one-footed one)! O you of a thousand undertakings! O great-headed one! O thousand-eyed one! O thousand-footed one! O iron-faced one! O <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being)! O thousand-armed one! O thousand-formed one! O thousand-eyed one! O source of thousands! The knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>, the best knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>, declare you a thousand-fold; they declare the universality of all things [to be you]. O you of flower-laughter! The supreme coursing is indeed the <s>Vauṣaṭ</s> exclamation! O <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>! O <s>Svāhā</s>! The one who receives his share in sacrifices, of a hundred streams and a thousand streams! You are indeed <s>Bhūḥ</s> and <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>! O you consisting of <s>Brahman</s>! O you devoted to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>! O <s>Brahmā</s>! You are the directions! You are the sky! You are the earth! You are <s>Mātariśvan</s> (wind)! You are the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker)! The <s>Potṛ</s> (purifier)! The <s>Mantṛ</s> (counselor)! The <s>Netṛ</s> (leader)! You alone are the foremost cause of oblation! By the splendor of the universe, you alone [shine]! By the directions, you are the one to be worshipped with garland-vessels! You are the altar! You are the kindling! You alone! You are the refuge of the wise! You are <s>Yoga</s>! You are <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation)! You are the supreme! You are the sacrificial ladle! You are the creator! You are the sacrifice! You are <s>Soma</s>! You are the smoke! You are the <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration)! You are the <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee)! You are the universe! O ancient one! O <s>Turāṣāḍ</s> (victorious)! O <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (golden embryo)! O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>! O <s>Ananta</s> (infinite one)! O you equal to a bull! O you of solar radiance! O you of solar splendor! O <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>! O <s>Puruṣottama</s> (supreme being)! O primordial god! O <s>Padmanābha</s>! O lotus-laughter! O you who recline on the lotus! O lotus-eyed one! O you with golden-tipped hair! O bright one! O soul of the universe! O god of the universe! O you whose face is everywhere! O you called the universe! O you from whom the universe is born! You alone are the consumer of the universe, O wide-strider, O transcender of the earth, O light-maker, O <s>Śambhu</s>, O self-born one of the heavens! O origin of beings! O great element! O you who pervade the universe! You are the universe itself! You are the protector of the universe! You are the purifier! You are the oblation! O sustainer of the universe! O you whose deeds are upward! O foremost of immortality! O guardian of the worlds! O you anointed with ghee! O <s>Agni</s>! O <s>Druhiṇa</s>! O you of infinite deeds! O you to whom all submit! O you whose sides are the universe! O <s>Pārśva</s>! You alone — O universe, protect those who seek boons, [saying] 'save us!'

children.translated_text: In the middle thereof, one should draw an eight-petaled lotus. Then one should divide it by a square layout raised from [the center], with four gates.

children.text: tatra madhye 'ṣṭa-patraṃ padmam ālikhet / tatas tu udāhṛta-catur-asrayā catur-dvāra-lekhayā vibhajet //
tataḥ padmakarṇikāmadhye śvetaṃ śatapatraṃ padmaṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: Then, in the middle of the lotus-pericarp, one should meditate on a white, hundred-petaled lotus.

children.text: tataḥ padma-karṇikā-madhye śvetaṃ śata-patraṃ padmaṃ dhyāyet //
tatkarṇikopary arkamaṇḍala[ṃ] / tadupari candramaṇḍala[ṃ] / tadupar[y] agnimaṇḍala[ṃ] / tanmadhye paraṃ puruṣam aśarīram agandham arasam arūpam asparśam aśabdaṃ sarvagaṃ plutāntaṃ oṃkāraṃ vinyaset //
children.translated_text: Upon its pericarp, the disc of the Sun; above that, the disc of the Moon; above that, the disc of Fire; in the middle of that, one should place the Supreme Person (<s>Paraṃ Puruṣam</s>) — bodiless, without smell, without taste, without form, without touch, without sound, all-pervading — the <s>Oṃkāra</s> (sacred syllable Oṃ) with the <s>pluta</s> (prolonged) ending.

children.text: tat-karṇika-upary arka-maṇḍala[ṃ] / tad-upari candramaṇḍala[ṃ] / tad-upar[y] agni-maṇḍala[ṃ] / tan-madhye paraṃ puruṣam aśarīram agandham arasam arūpam asparśam aśabdaṃ sarvagaṃ pluta-antaṃ oṃ-kāraṃ vinyaset //
kamalapūrvadale akāraṃ vāsudevaṃ nyaset / śvetavarṇaṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: On the eastern petal of the lotus, one should place the letter 'a' [representing] <s>Vāsudeva</s>; one should meditate [on him] as white in color.

children.text: kamala-pūrva-dale a-kāraṃ vāsudevaṃ nyaset / śveta-varṇaṃ dhyāyet //
dakṣiṇe ākāraṃ saṃkarṣaṇaṃ vinyaset / padmapatrābhaṃ taṃ ca dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: On the southern [petal], one should place the letter 'ā' [representing] <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>; one should meditate on him as having the lustre of a lotus petal.

children.text: dakṣiṇe ā-kāraṃ saṃkarṣaṇaṃ vinyaset / padma-patra-ābhaṃ taṃ ca dhyāyet //
paścime dale oṃkār[aṃ] pradyumnaṃ vinyaset / pītavarṇaṃ ca dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: On the western petal, one should place the <s>Oṃkāra</s> [representing] <s>Pradyumna</s>; one should meditate [on him] as yellow in color.

children.text: paścime dale oṃ-kār[aṃ] pradyumnaṃ vinyaset / pīta-varṇaṃ ca dhyāyet //
uttaradale aḥkāram aniruddhaṃ vinyaset / kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ ca dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: On the northern petal, one should place the letter 'aḥ' [representing] <s>Aniruddha</s>; one should meditate [on him] as dark in color.

children.text: uttara-dale aḥ-kāram aniruddhaṃ vinyaset / kṛṣṇa-varṇaṃ ca dhyāyet //
aiśāne dale tad iti brahmāṇaṃ vinyaset / padmapatrābhaṃ dhyāyet // [Vdha_3.352.0.9] //
children.translated_text: On the northeastern petal, one should place 'tat' [representing] <s>Brahmā</s>; one should meditate [on him] as having the lustre of a lotus petal.

children.text: aiśāne dale tad iti brahmāṇaṃ vinyaset / padma-patra-ābhaṃ dhyāyet // [Vdha_3.352.0.9] //

children.translated_text: [...]; one should meditate [on it] as equal to ten million suns.
On the northwestern petal, one should place the Boar (<s>Varāha</s>); one should meditate [on him] as resembling crushed collyrium.

children.text:
prapūrvadvāre oṃ keṃ ṭeṃ yeṃ etāny akṣarāṇi vainateyaṃ vinyaset /
hemavarṇaṃ ca dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: At the front eastern gate, one should place the syllables 'oṃ keṃ ṭeṃ yeṃ' [representing] <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>); one should meditate [on him] as golden in color.

children.text:
prapūrva-dvāre oṃ keṃ ṭeṃ yeṃ etāny akṣarāṇi vainateyaṃ vinyaset /
hema-varṇaṃ ca dhyāyet //
dakṣiṇe dvāre tejoratharatṛ(?)cakraṃ sudarśanaṃ vinyaset / vajranābhaṃ sahasrāraṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabhaṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: At the southern gate, one should place the discus <s>Sudarśana</s>, the chariot of splendor; one should meditate [on it] as having a diamond hub, a thousand spokes, and radiance equal to ten million suns.

children.text: dakṣiṇe dvāre tejo-ratharatṛ(?)-cakraṃ sudarśanaṃ vinyaset / vajra-nābhaṃ sahasra-araṃ sūryakoṭi-sama-prabhaṃ dhyāyet //

children.translated_text: At the western gate, one should place the bow <s>Śārṅga</s>; one should meditate [on it] as resembling <s>Indra</s>'s rainbow.

children.text: sveṃ ṭheṃ heṃ theṃ uttare dvāre aniruddhaṃ nyasyet / sarvavarṇaṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: With [the syllables] 'sveṃ ṭheṃ heṃ theṃ,' at the northern gate, one should place <s>Aniruddha</s>; one should meditate [on him] as of all colors.

children.text: sveṃ ṭheṃ heṃ theṃ uttare dvāre aniruddhaṃ nyasyet / sarva-varṇaṃ dhyāyet //
veṃ ṇeṃ kṣeṃ kṣeṃ vidikṣu pāñcajanyaṃ śaṅkhaṃ nyaset / śaśāṅkavarṇaṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: With [the syllables] 'veṃ ṇeṃ kṣeṃ kṣeṃ,' in the intermediate directions, one should place the conch <s>Pāñcajanya</s>; one should meditate [on it] as moon-colored.

children.text: veṃ ṇeṃ kṣeṃ kṣeṃ vidikṣu pāñca-janyaṃ śaṅkhaṃ nyaset / śaśa-aṅka-varṇaṃ dhyāyet //
dheṃ heṃ bheṃ heṃ śriyaṃ padmaṃ dakṣiṇato nyaset / śuklāṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: With [the syllables] 'dheṃ heṃ bheṃ heṃ,' one should place <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of prosperity) with a lotus, to the south; one should meditate [on her] as white.

children.text: dheṃ heṃ bheṃ heṃ śriyaṃ padmaṃ dakṣiṇato nyaset / śuklāṃ dhyāyet //
geṃ ḍeṃ veṃ śeṃ padmāntarataḥ puṣṭiṃ nyaset / śvetāṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: With [the syllables] 'geṃ ḍeṃ veṃ śeṃ,' within the lotus, one should place <s>Puṣṭi</s> (Nourishment); one should meditate [on her] as white.

children.text: geṃ ḍeṃ veṃ śeṃ padma-antarataḥ puṣṭiṃ nyaset / śvetāṃ dhyāyet //
heṃ seṃ purato vanamālāṃ nyaset / heṃ seṃ bahuvarṇāṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: <s>heṃ seṃ</s> — one should place the <s>vanamālā</s> (forest garland) in front. <s>heṃ seṃ</s> — one should meditate on it as multicolored.

children.text: heṃ seṃ purato vana-mālāṃ nyaset / heṃ seṃ bahu-varṇāṃ dhyāyet //

children.translated_text: In the northeast of the altar, one should place <s>Nandaka</s> (the sword). One should meditate on it as sky-colored.

children.text: oṃ ity āgneyyāṃ varma nyaset / bahuvarṇaṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: <s>oṃ</s> — in the southeast, one should place the armor. One should meditate on it as multicolored.

children.text: oṃ ity āgneyyāṃ varma nyaset / bahu-varṇaṃ dhyāyet //
oṃ jheṃ leṃ śrīvatsaṃ nyaset / śukl[a]ṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: <s>oṃ jheṃ leṃ</s> — one should place the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> (auspicious mark). One should meditate on it as white.

children.text: oṃ jheṃ leṃ śrīvatsaṃ nyaset / śukl[a]ṃ dhyāyet //
oṃ cheṃ ṭheṃ vāyavye kaustubhaṃ nyaset / ādityaṃ dīptaṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: <s>oṃ cheṃ ṭheṃ</s> — in the northwest, one should place the <s>Kaustubha</s> (jewel). One should meditate on it as blazing like the sun.

children.text: oṃ cheṃ ṭheṃ vāyavye kaustubhaṃ nyaset / ādityaṃ dīptaṃ dhyāyet //
tato maṇḍale bāhyasthāṃ yathāsvadiśam okāraukārau (?) dikpatī śakrāgnī yamanairṛtavāruṇapavanakuberān aiśānyāṃ nyaset / yathoktarūpaṃ dhyāyet //
children.translated_text: Then, outside the <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual diagram), in their respective directions, one should place the <s>oṃ</s> and <s>auṃ</s> syllables, the guardians of the directions — <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Nairṛta</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Pavana</s>, <s>Kubera</s> — and in the northeast. One should meditate on them in their prescribed forms.

children.text: tato maṇḍale bāhya-sthāṃ yathā-sva-diśam o-kārau-kārau (?) dik-patī śakra-agnī yama-nairṛta-vāruṇa-pavana-kuberān aiśānyāṃ nyaset / yatha-ukta-rūpaṃ dhyāyet //
oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāyety antena dvādaśākṣareṇa karṇikāmadhye puruṣāyārghyapādyācamanīyānulepanapuṣpadīpadhūpamadhuparkanaivedyaphalabhakṣyāṇi nivedayet //
children.translated_text: With the twelve-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] ending in '<s>oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya</s>,' one should offer to the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) at the center of the pericarp: <s>arghya</s> (water offering), <s>pādya</s> (water for washing feet), <s>ācamanīya</s> (water for sipping), <s>anulepa</s> (ointment), <s>puṣpa</s> (flowers), <s>dīpa</s> (lamp), <s>dhūpa</s> (incense), <s>madhuparka</s> (honey mixture), <s>naivedya</s> (food offering), fruits, and edibles.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya ity antena dvādaśa-akṣareṇa karṇikā-madhye puruṣāya arghya-pādya-ācamanīya-anulepana-puṣpa-dīpa-dhūpa-madhu-parka-naivedya-phala-bhakṣyāṇi nivedayet //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāyety athavāṣṭākṣareṇa mantreṇa / oṃ jitaṃ te puṇḍarīkākṣa namas te viśvabhāvana / manas te 'stu hṛṣīkeśa mahāpuruṣa pūrvaja //
children.translated_text: Or with the eight-syllable <s>mantra</s> '<s>oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya</s>.' [Or with:] '<s>oṃ</s> — Victory to you, O lotus-eyed one! Salutations to you, O creator of the universe! May [my] mind be [devoted] to you, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, O Great Being, O Primordial One!'

children.text: oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya ity athava āṣṭa-akṣareṇa mantreṇa / oṃ jitaṃ te puṇḍarīkākṣa namas te viśva-bhāvana / manas te 'stu hṛṣīkeśa mahā-puruṣa pūrvaja //
ity anena mantreṇa puruṣasūktena vā / athānyān dalaniviṣṭān devān yathābhihitair mantraiḥ pṛthakpṛthag arcaye[t] //
children.translated_text: With this <s>mantra</s>, or with the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>. Then one should worship the other deities situated on the petals, each separately with their respective prescribed <s>mantras</s>.

children.text: ity anena mantreṇa puruṣa-sūktena vā / atha anyān dala-niviṣṭān devān yathā-abhihitair mantraiḥ pṛthak-pṛthag arcaye[t] //

ārogyaṃ dhanadhānyavardhanaṃ śatrughnaṃ vaśīkaraṇaṃ yaḥ puruṣo 'nena vidhinā satataṃ devam abhyarcayati saṃpattiṃ janayati athavā tasya na rocate tadā śvetadvīpam avpyāpya arkamaṇḍalaṃ bhittvā niruṇaddhi pradyumnasaṃkarṣaṇān prāpnoti sudevatvam avāpya niṣkalatvam āpnoti //
children.translated_text: It grants health, increase of wealth and grain, destruction of enemies, and subjugation. The person who constantly worships the deity by this rite generates prosperity. Or if he does not desire that, then having pervaded <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island) and piercing the orb of the sun, he attains [union with] <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, and having attained supreme divinity, he reaches the state of being without parts (<s>niṣkalatva</s>).
